exposure: Age of onset (neonatal vs. infantile type)
Clinical characteristics (seizures, lethargy, hypotonia, apnea, feeble sobbing)
Genetic analysis (GLDC, AMT gene abnormalities and new variations)
Cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings (abnormal signals, dysplasia of corpus callosum, white matter abnormalities)
Electroencephalography (EEG) examinations (burst suppression, hypsarrhythmia, epileptic activity)
cohort: The study included 20 Chinese patients diagnosed with Nonketotic Hyperglycinemia (NKH), 17 with the neonatal type and 3 with the infantile type.
finding: The study found diverse disease processes and outcomes in Chinese NKH patients, with 85% having the neonatal type, 50% mortality overall (with 8 deaths in the neonatal period), and varying developmental disorders among survivors.
